title: Add "Add to Cart" Button on Product Listing Page
stack: React 18 + Redux Toolkit + react-toastify + axios (frontend); Node/Express-style REST backend contract; Jest + React Testing Library
notes: Layer mapping for this React/Redux stack (schema enum is controller|service|repository|dto): controller = REST API endpoint/contract and UI components that receive user events and delegate; service = src/services modules and Redux thunks (business logic, API client); repository = storage/state layer (localStorage via cartStorage, Redux slices as the in-memory store, static catalogue data); dto = request/response payload shapes and validators. Spring Boot guidance in arch_instructions.md was intentionally not applied; the run targets the existing React + Redux + Jest repo. ACs 1, 5 and 6 are mainly client-side: they are covered by UI components plus the 'CLIENT' pseudo-endpoint entry (not a real HTTP route). state/memory.json was empty, so no learned patterns were applied.

components.name: ProductList
components.responsibility: src/components/ProductList.jsx. Renders the product catalogue grid from the catalogue source (src/data/products.js now, GET /api/products later) and one ProductCard per product. Handles empty/error states. Covers AC 1.

components.name: ProductCard
components.responsibility: src/components/ProductCard.jsx. Presentational card (name, price, safe image) that always includes an AddToCartButton for every product. Text is rendered via React escaping only (no dangerouslySetInnerHTML); imageUrl must pass isSafeImageUrl (http/https only). Covers AC 1.

components.name: AddToCartButton
components.responsibility: src/components/AddToCartButton.jsx. Per-product button with states idle ('Add to Cart'), adding (disabled, aria-busy), added ('Added ✓' for about 2s, then reset), error ('Try again') and out_of_stock (disabled, label 'Out of Stock'). Dispatches the addToCart thunk, shows toast 'Item added to cart!' on success and a generic toast on failure, announces success via an aria-live region. Covers AC 1, 2, 3, 5.

components.name: Header
components.responsibility: src/components/Header.jsx. Site header containing the CartIcon; the place where the live cart count is visible. Covers AC 4.

components.name: CartIcon
components.responsibility: src/components/CartIcon.jsx. Subscribes to the Redux cart count selector and renders the badge with an accessible label (e.g. 'Cart, N items'). Re-renders immediately on state change so the counter updates in real time without a page reload. Covers AC 4.

components.name: App
components.responsibility: src/App.jsx / src/index.jsx. Composition root: Redux Provider, ToastContainer, Header and ProductList. On mount hydrates the guest cart from localStorage (hydrateGuestCart) so the counter is correct after reload. Covers AC 4, 6.

components.name: cartSlice
components.responsibility: src/store/cartSlice.js. Redux Toolkit slice holding items, count, statusByProduct and a safe error. The addToCart async thunk validates input first, then branches on authentication (logged-in: API via cartService; guest: localStorage via cartStorage) and returns only schema-validated items/count. Reducers hydrateGuestCart and resetAddStatus. Single source of truth for the header counter. Covers AC 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7.

components.name: authSlice
components.responsibility: src/store/authSlice.js. Holds only a boolean isAuthenticated flag set by the host app's login flow (assumed contract). No tokens, passwords or user PII are stored in client state; the session is carried by an HttpOnly cookie. Covers AC 6, 7.

components.name: store
components.responsibility: src/store/index.js. configureStore combining cart and auth reducers (Redux DevTools disabled in production builds). Covers AC 4.

components.name: cartService
components.responsibility: src/services/cartService.js. axios client (baseURL from REACT_APP_API_BASE_URL env var, withCredentials, 10s timeout) exposing addItem(productId, quantity) -> POST /api/cart/add. Validates input before sending; maps HTTP errors (400, 401, 409, 5xx/network) to a CartError carrying only a safe user-facing message. Covers AC 2, 5, 7.

components.name: cartStorage
components.responsibility: src/services/cartStorage.js. Guest cart persistence in window.localStorage under key 'guest_cart' (assumption: localStorage rather than sessionStorage). loadGuestCart validates the JSON schema and returns [] on corrupt/tampered data; saveGuestCart validates before write and survives quota/security errors; addGuestItem merges quantities capped at MAX_QUANTITY (99) and MAX_CART_ENTRIES (100). Covers AC 6.

components.name: validators
components.responsibility: src/utils/validators.js. Shared validation for the cart payload DTO: productId matches /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/, quantity is an integer 1..99, cart schema (array max 100 of {productId, quantity}), and isSafeImageUrl (http/https only). Used identically by UI, thunk, service and storage. Covers AC 2, 6, 7.

components.name: AddToCartRequestDTO
components.responsibility: Request payload for POST /api/cart/add: { productId: string (^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$), quantity: integer 1..99 }. The server must re-validate (client validation is not trusted). Covers AC 2, 7.

components.name: CartResponseDTO
components.responsibility: Response payload: { items: [{ productId, quantity }], count: integer >= 0 }. The client re-validates it with validateCartSchema and falls back to a locally computed count; unknown fields are ignored. Covers AC 2, 4, 7.

components.name: productsCatalogue
components.responsibility: src/data/products.js. Synthetic catalogue ({ id, name, price, imageUrl, inStock }) used until a catalogue API exists; inStock drives the Out of Stock state. Synthetic data only. Covers AC 1, 5.

components.name: CartApi (backend)
components.responsibility: Assumed Node/Express backend (outside this repo's src/). Authenticates the session cookie, re-validates the payload, checks stock server-side, persists the cart for the user in the database using parameterized queries/ORM only, and returns CartResponseDTO. Covers AC 2, 4, 5, 7.

endpoints.access: Authenticated (logged-in users only); session via HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookie. Guests never call this endpoint.

responses.200: Item added; body { items: [{productId, quantity}], count } with the authoritative cart count used to update the header (AC 2, 3, 4, 7).
responses.400: Invalid productId/quantity or malformed JSON; generic message, no field-level internals.
responses.401: Not authenticated or session expired; client shows 'Your session has expired. Please sign in again.'
responses.409: Product out of stock (server-side authority for AC 5); client shows 'This item is out of stock.' and disables the button.
responses.429: Rate limit exceeded; client shows a generic retry message.
responses.500: Unexpected error; generic message only, no stack trace or internals.

endpoints.access: Authenticated (logged-in users only). Assumed endpoint, not in the Jira ticket.

responses.200: Current server-side cart { items, count } fetched after login/page load so the header counter reflects the DB-synced cart (AC 4, 7).

endpoints.access: Authenticated (logged-in users only). Assumed optional endpoint; flagged as an open question.

request.items: array (max 100) of { productId, quantity } validated like AddToCartRequestDTO

responses.200: Guest cart items merged into the user's server cart (quantities summed, capped at 99); client then calls clearGuestCart() and replaces state with the returned { items, count }.

endpoints.access: Public. Assumed endpoint; today the catalogue is the static src/data/products.js.

responses.200: List of { id, name, price, imageUrl, inStock }; one ProductCard each with an Add to Cart button on every card (AC 1); inStock=false renders a disabled 'Out of Stock' button (AC 5).
responses.500: Generic error; ProductList shows a safe error state.

endpoints.access: Guest (not authenticated). Pseudo-endpoint representing the client-only guest flow handled by cartStorage; no network call is made.

responses.success: Item merged into the validated guest cart in localStorage, Redux count updated, toast and 'Added ✓' shown (AC 2, 3, 4, 6).
responses.INVALID_INPUT: Rejected before write; generic error toast.
responses.CART_FULL: More than 100 distinct entries; rejected with a generic error.
responses.STORAGE_FAILED: Quota/security error writing localStorage; generic error toast, cart state is not falsely incremented.

ui_behavior_mapping.criterion: Add to Cart button visible on every product card
ui_behavior_mapping.behavior: ProductList maps every product to a ProductCard and every ProductCard always renders an AddToCartButton (including out-of-stock items, where it is disabled).
Click dispatches addToCart; authenticated users hit POST /api/cart/add, guests write localStorage.
react-toastify success toast 'Item added to cart!' plus button state 'Added ✓' for about 2s and an aria-live announcement.

ui_behavior_mapping.criterion: Header cart counter updates in real time
ui_behavior_mapping.behavior: CartIcon selects cart.count; the slice updates synchronously on fulfilled, so the header re-renders without reload. Count is hydrated from localStorage (guest) or GET /api/cart (logged-in) on load.
getButtonState(inStock=false) returns disabled 'Out of Stock'; the click handler returns early; a 409 from the API also moves the button to out_of_stock.

ui_behavior_mapping.criterion: Guest cart stored in local storage/session
ui_behavior_mapping.behavior: When isAuthenticated is false the thunk uses addGuestItem (localStorage key 'guest_cart'); App hydrates it on load.

ui_behavior_mapping.criterion: Logged-in cart syncs with backend DB
ui_behavior_mapping.behavior: When isAuthenticated is true the thunk calls POST /api/cart/add and replaces state with the server's authoritative { items, count }; on login the guest cart is merged via POST /api/cart/merge (assumed) and cleared locally.

security_controls: Input validation (client and server): productId must match ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$ and quantity must be an integer 1..99; enforced in the addToCart thunk, cartService and cartStorage, and re-validated server-side in /api/cart/add and /api/cart/merge. Reject unknown fields and payloads over a small size limit (for example 10 KB).

AuthN for logged-in sync: /api/cart/add, /api/cart and /api/cart/merge require an authenticated session (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookie; axios withCredentials). The client authSlice stores only a boolean, never tokens or credentials. The server derives the user from the session, never from a client-supplied userId (prevents IDOR / broken access control).
AuthZ: users can only read or modify their own cart; no cart or user identifier is accepted in the path or body.

XSS-safe rendering: product name, price and toast text are rendered through React's default escaping; dangerouslySetInnerHTML is forbidden; toast messages are fixed constants, never server-supplied strings; imageUrl is rendered only if isSafeImageUrl passes (http/https, no javascript: or data: URLs).

Safe localStorage handling: stored data is untrusted; loadGuestCart parses in try/catch and validates the full schema (max 100 entries, validated fields) and returns [] on any failure; only productId/quantity are stored (no PII, prices, tokens or session data); writes are wrapped in try/catch for quota/security errors; prices are never trusted from client storage (server recomputes).
Server-side authority for stock and price: out-of-stock is enforced server-side (409) in addition to the UI disabling the button; a client-supplied price is never accepted.

No secrets in code: the API base URL comes from the REACT_APP_API_BASE_URL environment variable; no keys, tokens or credentials in src/ or design artifacts; backend DB/session secrets come from environment variables or a secret manager. Only non-secret REACT_APP_* values are exposed to the browser bundle.

Safe error messages: the client maps all failures to fixed messages (e.g. 'Could not add item. Please try again.'); server error bodies, stack traces, SQL or internal codes are never displayed or returned; the backend returns generic bodies with correlation IDs only.

No PII or secrets in logs: the client does not console.log cart payloads or errors in production; the backend logs only productId, quantity, an opaque user reference and a correlation ID; never cookies, session IDs, addresses or emails.

CSRF: because the API uses cookie auth, require SameSite cookies plus a CSRF token header (double-submit or synchronizer token) or a strict Origin/Referer check on state-changing POSTs; enforce JSON-only Content-Type; CORS allow-list of the known frontend origin only (no wildcard with credentials).

Rate limiting and abuse control: per-user/IP rate limit on POST /api/cart/add and /api/cart/merge (429 on exceed); the client disables the button while a request is in flight (status 'adding') to prevent double-submits; cart size capped at 100 entries and 99 per item.
Injection: the backend uses parameterized queries or an ORM only for cart persistence; no string-concatenated SQL/NoSQL; the JSON body is parsed with a schema validator.
Transport and headers: HTTPS only (HSTS), Secure cookies, Content-Security-Policy restricting script-src to self and img-src to approved image hosts, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.
Dependency hygiene: pin versions in package.json/lockfile and run npm audit in CI to address vulnerable components (OWASP A06).
Request timeout (10s) and generic fallbacks so failed or slow calls cannot leave the UI stuck in the 'adding' state.
Synthetic data only: catalogue and test fixtures use demo data; no real customer data.

owasp_checklist.location: CartApi (backend) persistence; client has no SQL
owasp_checklist.fix: Backend must use ORM/prepared statements and schema-validate the body.

owasp_checklist.check: 2. Input validation on every request DTO
owasp_checklist.fix: Mirror the same rules server-side (Bean-Validation equivalent such as Joi/zod/express-validator).
n/a; the auth mechanism is tracked as an open question.

owasp_checklist.location: cartService REACT_APP_API_BASE_URL; design.json contains no secrets

owasp_checklist.fix: Enforce in backend logging config and code review.

threats.threat: A01 Broken Access Control / IDOR: attacker modifies another user's cart by supplying a userId or cartId
threats.mitigation: No user or cart identifiers accepted from the client; the server derives the user from the authenticated session; every query is scoped to that user.

threats.threat: A03 Injection: malicious productId/quantity reaching the DB (SQL/NoSQL injection)
threats.mitigation: Strict allow-list regex and integer range validation on client and server; parameterized queries/ORM only; unknown fields rejected.

threats.threat: A03 XSS: product name/imageUrl or server messages containing script, or javascript: image URLs
threats.mitigation: React escaping only, no dangerouslySetInnerHTML; fixed-constant toast text; isSafeImageUrl allows http/https only; Content-Security-Policy.

threats.threat: A04/A08 Insecure design / tampering of the localStorage guest cart (edited quantity, prices, huge payloads, malformed JSON)
threats.mitigation: Treat localStorage as untrusted: full schema validation with size caps, fall back to an empty cart, store no prices; the server recomputes price and stock when the cart is merged or checked out.

threats.threat: A01/A05 CSRF on state-changing cart endpoints using cookie auth
threats.mitigation: SameSite cookies, CSRF token or Origin check, JSON Content-Type enforced, CORS allow-list without wildcard.

threats.threat: A07 Identification and Authentication Failures: expired/forged session used for cart sync
threats.mitigation: The server validates the session on every call and returns 401; the client shows a generic re-login message and does not fall back to unauthenticated server writes; no tokens kept in JS-readable storage.

threats.threat: A05 Security Misconfiguration / information disclosure via verbose errors
threats.mitigation: Generic client-facing messages mapped in mapError; the backend returns generic bodies and logs details server-side only; production builds without source maps or DevTools.

threats.threat: A09 Logging failures / sensitive data exposure in logs
threats.mitigation: Log only opaque identifiers, productId, quantity and a correlation ID; never cookies, tokens or emails; no console logging of payloads in the client.

threats.threat: Denial of service / abuse: automated add-to-cart flooding or oversized guest cart
threats.mitigation: Per-user and IP rate limiting (429), in-flight button lock, 100-entry and 99-quantity caps, request size limit and 10s client timeout.

threats.threat: A06 Vulnerable and outdated components (axios, react-scripts, react-toastify)
threats.mitigation: Lockfile, npm audit/dependabot in CI, minimal dependency set.

threats.threat: Stock bypass: attacker re-enables the disabled Out of Stock button via DevTools and posts the add request
threats.mitigation: The server re-checks inventory and returns 409; the UI is not the authority for stock.

threats.threat: A02 Cryptographic failures: cart or session data intercepted in transit
threats.mitigation: HTTPS/HSTS only, Secure and HttpOnly cookies; no sensitive data stored in localStorage.

assumptions: Guest storage is localStorage (key 'guest_cart') rather than sessionStorage so the guest cart persists across tabs and browser restarts; the spec's 'local storage/session' wording is ambiguous.

API contract assumed: POST /api/cart/add accepts { productId, quantity } and returns { items: [{productId, quantity}], count }; status codes 400/401/403/404/409/429/500 as listed. GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart/merge and GET /api/products are assumed additions and not part of the ticket.
Authentication is a session cookie (HttpOnly) managed by the host app's login flow; the frontend only holds an isAuthenticated boolean (authSlice) and sends credentials with withCredentials.
Out-of-stock is conveyed by product.inStock=false from the catalogue and by HTTP 409 from /api/cart/add.
Default quantity per click is 1; the maximum per product is 99 and 100 distinct entries per cart (design limits, not from the ticket).
Epic 'Shopping Cart & Checkout' and Jira priority 'Medium' are taken from spec.json as given; the Jira field is treated as authoritative over the description text.
Responsive behavior (desktop and mobile) is handled in src/styles.css and verified by tests; there is no separate mobile component tree.
All data is synthetic (demo catalogue); no real customer data is used.
open_questions: Priority mismatch: Jira priority field is 'Medium' but the description text states 'Priority: High'. Jira field value used.
Epic: the Jira 'parent' field was not returned; epic 'Shopping Cart & Checkout' is taken from the description text. Also, the Jira issue type is returned as 'Epic' while the description says 'Story'.

Technical notes/Definition of Done in the ticket (not acceptance criteria): API endpoint /api/cart/add must be integrated; unit tests for In stock, Out of stock and Success states; tested on desktop and mobile responsive views.
Backend contract for /api/cart/add (request/response schema, auth for logged-in users) is not specified. Design assumes the contract listed in 'assumptions'.
Guest storage choice is ambiguous ('local storage/session'): localStorage or sessionStorage is not decided. Design assumes localStorage.
Guest-to-logged-in cart merge on login is not specified in the ACs: should guest items merge into the server cart (assumed POST /api/cart/merge), replace it, or be discarded?
Should adding an item already in the cart increment its quantity (assumed) or be rejected, and what is the per-item maximum (assumed 99)?
Which CSRF mechanism and CORS origin policy does the backend use (token header vs. Origin check)?
